subject: Linguistics
title: Universal Grammar Debate
description: A quick win: understand Universal Grammar Debate.

hook.text: Chomsky claimed all languages share a deep structural blueprint—a Universal Grammar.

buildup.text: The idea explains how children learn language so fast: much of the structure is pre-installed.

discovery.text: Supporters point to cross-linguistic universals: all languages have nouns and verbs, subjects and predicates.

twist.text: Critics point to radical exceptions—Pirahã challenges recursion, Riau challenges fixed categories.

climax.text: After sixty years the debate is unresolved—and it remains one of linguistics' biggest questions.

punchline.text: Is grammar born or learned? The jury is still out.

quiz.question: What is Universal Grammar?
options: An innate structural blueprint shared by all languages
A grammar textbook for all languages
